chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jamhur from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam from al-Haytham ibn Waqid from Muhammad ibn Suleman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said:

He said: Indeed, the hypocrite forbids but does not keep away (from what he forbids), and he commands what he does not perform; and when he stands for prayer, he turns around. I said: O son of the Messenger of Allah, and what is the turning around? He said: The turning around.

And when he bows, he crouches; in the evening his concern is dinner although he has not fasted, and in the morning his concern is sleep although he has not stayed awake (in worship). If he narrates to you, he lies; and if you entrust him, he betrays you; and if you are absent, he backbites you; and if he promises you, he breaks it.

key_terms.الِالْتِفَاتُ: Turning around (a sign of haste or distraction in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical and behavioral signs of a hypocrite according to Imam Ali (as)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the lineage of Imam Ali al-Rida, provides a detailed phenomenological description of the hypocrite's spiritual dissonance, particularly in the ritual of prayer where physical movements lack inner presence. It expands on the concept of *Nifaq* by linking external religious performance with internal moral corruption, such as backbiting and broken promises, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unity of belief and action.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asammi, from Al Haysam Bin Waqid, form Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws having said: ‘They hypocrite forbids and he does not keep away (himself), and he orders with what he does not perform; and when he stands to the Salāt, raises objections’.
I said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! And what is the ‘raising objections’?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The turning around.

And when he performs Ruku’u, he crouches, and in the evening he thinks of the dinner although he did not Fast, and in the morning he thinks of the sleep although he did not stay awake worshipping at night. If he were to narrate to you, he would lie, and if you were to entrust him, he would betray you, and if you are absent, he would backbite you, and if he promises you, he would break it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-‘Assam from al-Haytham ibn Waqid from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from ibn Muskan from abu Hamza from Ali ibn al- Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) has said, ‘

A hypocrite forbids others, but himself does not desist from prohibited matters and commands others with what he himself does not perform. When prayer is to begin he (7 ’tarazd) avoids it.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘O descendent of the messenger of Allah, “What is ‘I’tirazT’ The Imam said, ‘It is turning away. When he is in the Ruku’ position (kneeling) he uses it as resting place. Toward the evening his only concern is dinner, even though he is not fasting. Toward morning his only concern is more sleep, even though he has not passed the night awake worshipping. If he speaks to you, he lies. If you trust him, he breaches it. Behind your back, he backbites you and if he promises you, he disregards his promise.’”
